units.t: Statistics: Tally Charts and Frequency Tables

unit.title: Fractions of Shapes
unit.blurb: Halves, quarters, thirds, fifths and tenths of shapes, unit and non-unit fractions, and simple equivalent fractions.
unit.subject: maths

O1.t: Understand that a fraction is equal parts of a whole and name unit and non-unit fractions of shapes.

O2.t: Recognise that two fractions can be equivalent, such as 1/2 = 2/4.

p: A fraction is **equal parts** of a whole. A circle cut into 4 equal parts shows **quarters**. One part is **1/4**.
**3/4** means 3 of the 4 equal parts. The bottom number (denominator) is how many equal parts; the top number (numerator) is how many we have.
If the parts are not equal, they are not quarters.

p: **1/2 = 2/4**: half a circle covers the same amount as two quarters.
2/4 has more parts than 1/2, but the parts are smaller, so the amount is the same.

req.model: If you cut each half of a shape into two equal pieces, you get quarters. One half becomes two quarters, but the shaded amount is the same, so 1/2 = 2/4.
req.reason: If you cut each half of a shape into two equal pieces, you get quarters. One half becomes two quarters, but the shaded amount is the same, so 1/2 = 2/4.
